key_insight: By exploiting the fact that multiple objects in a single scene share the same illumination, MultiGP performs generative inverse rendering to stochastically disentangle reflectance, texture, and illumination from one image, yielding multiple plausible radiometric explanations.
problem_solved: Addresses the fundamentally ambiguous task of radiometric disentanglement from a single image — recovering object materials (reflectance and texture) and scene illumination jointly and robustly.
method: Generative inverse rendering that samples full radiometric constituents (reflectance, texture, illumination) to produce multiple plausible explanations for observed appearance.
Enforces a cross-object consensus constraint: different objects may have different materials/textures but are constrained to share the same scene illumination.
Probabilistic/stochastic sampling to capture ambiguity and present diverse plausible reconstructions rather than a single deterministic estimate.
impact: Enables more reliable single-image material and lighting estimation with uncertainty-aware outputs, improving downstream tasks like relighting, material editing, AR compositing, and scene understanding.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input single image → generative inverse renderer → sampled outputs (reflectance maps, textures, environment illumination).
Comparison grid: multiple sampled reconstructions showing different plausible material/illumination decompositions.
Schematic illustrating the shared-illumination constraint across several objects in the scene (arrows converging to one illumination map).
Before/after examples: object relighting or material swap using recovered illumination and materials.
paper_title: Under One Sun: Multi-Object Generative Perception of Materials and Illumination
paper_authors: Nobuo Yoshii, Xinran Nicole Han, Ryo Kawahara, Todd Zickler, Ko Nishino
